## Opposite, zero and unit vectors {#iv1-special .vector-lesson}

<div data-vector="special" class="v-interactive"></div>

<div class="v-definitions">
<p><strong>Opposite:</strong> <span data-math="-\mathbf a"></span> has the same magnitude and opposite direction.</p>
<p><strong>Zero:</strong> <span data-math="\mathbf0"></span> has magnitude zero and no direction.</p>
<p><strong>Unit:</strong> a vector with magnitude <span data-math="1"></span>. In the direction of non-zero <span data-math="\mathbf a"></span>, write <span data-math="\hat{\mathbf a}"></span>.</p>
</div>

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet §1.3 · p. 2</div>

::: notes
Switch between opposite, zero and unit. Reverse a without changing its length. The zero vector is represented by a point; it has magnitude zero, not an undefined magnitude. A unit vector can point in any direction; it need not be horizontal or vertical. Use the marked unit scale. Only define the unit vector now; the formula a/|a| belongs in revised Lesson 4. A zero vector has no associated direction or unit vector.
:::
